findings.heading: Data interoperability / Совместимость данных
findings.proposition: The English sentence carries a working cross-reference to the Import and export page (link target importing.qmd); the Russian writes the label [Импорт и экспорт] with no link target at all.
findings.reader_consequence: The Russian reader is told to see the Import and export page but has nothing to click, and the bracketed label renders as literal text, so the only pointer in the whole section leads nowhere.

findings.heading: Tidy data / Аккуратные данные
findings.proposition: The English says the status "TBC" sits in the same cell as "Partner D"; the Russian names that cell "Part112ner D", a string that does not exist in the figure.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader looks in the screenshot for a cell labelled "Part112ner D", cannot find it, and cannot verify the example of two pieces of information combined in one cell.

findings.heading: From Stata / Из Stata
findings.proposition: The English R-side says that converting a column to Factor class and specifying levels labels the VALUES; the Russian says it labels the variables ("Переменные подписываются").
findings.reader_consequence: A Stata user reads that R labels variables, which contradicts the very next Russian sentence saying column names are not usually labelled, so the value-label versus variable-label distinction that the row exists to teach is lost.

findings.heading: From SAS / Из SAS
findings.proposition: The English R-side says that converting a column to Factor class and specifying levels labels the VALUES; the Russian says it labels the variables ("Подпись переменных").
findings.reader_consequence: A SAS user reads that R labels variables, which contradicts the following Russian sentence saying column names are not usually labelled, and so misunderstands what factor levels label.

findings.heading: From SAS / Из SAS
findings.proposition: The English says the dplyr package offers a few functions for merging datasets; the Russian says dplyr offers NEW functions ("новые функции") for merging datasets.
findings.reader_consequence: The Russian reader is told the merge functions are new rather than that there are several of them, so the row no longer signals that a choice between several join functions must be made.
